gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies the invalid cut-boundary trace/interpolation step used to control the penalty flux term: the proof invokes a gradient-based estimate although only L2 and divergence approximation are assumed. This is the same failed boundary estimate that cannot support the advertised h^(2r) penalty-norm bound and instead leads to the boundary loss, including loss of the lowest-order convergence guarantee.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof does not possess the required boundary approximation/trace control for the H(div) interpolant, so the nonempty-flux-boundary penalty contribution cannot be bounded with the claimed optimal h-scaling; the resulting theorem must use the weakened boundary-dependent estimate or add a suitable supercloseness hypothesis.

component_coverage.gold_component: The nonempty-flux-boundary penalty term is estimated using an unsupported cut-trace/interpolation step, so the claimed h^(2r) scaling is not justified and loses one power of h.

component_coverage.gold_component: The resulting theorem and convergence prose must be qualified, with lowest-order Raviart–Thomas convergence no longer guaranteed in the affected boundary regime.
